settings.title: What Are Dye Lot Variations?
settings.text:
Dye lot variations are subtle differences in color that can occur between batches of fabric.
Industry standards allow up to a 6% color variation.

A dye lot is a group of textiles dyed in the same vat at the same time.

Despite careful dyeing techniques, slight differences can arise due to various factors like temperature, water quality, or differences in dye composition.

settings.title: Factors Influencing Dye Lot Differences
settings.text:
• Temperature: Variations in dye temperature affect final color.
  • Water Quality: Differences in water purity can alter fabric hue.
  • Dye Composition: Changes in pigment ratios influence color outcomes.
  • Yarn Base: Even similar yarn batches can yield varying results.
  • Dye Bath Ratios: Different ratios of hues impact the dye bath.
  • Barometric Pressure: Air pressure shifts can lead to variations.
  • Fabric Flow: How fabric moves within the dye bath affects consistency.

settings.title: Cozyology's Approach to Quality Control
settings.text:
To minimize color variations, Cozyology carefully manages the production process:

  1. Same Batch Consistency: We aim to use yarn from the same dye lot in each production run.
  2. Batch Coordination: Ensure that all fabrics in an order come from the same batch.
  3. Color Matching: Fabrics are matched meticulously to the original color card.

settings.title: Order Together
settings.text: Place a single order for drapes in a room to ensure consistent color and uniformity.

settings.title: Lighting Considerations
settings.text: Check fabric samples in the room's lighting where the curtains will be placed to ensure the color matches your desired look.
